# USB-C interface verification

**DESIGN HOLD — passive interface implemented; electrical qualification pending.** Generated by `npm run check:interface` from exact native
PCB/schematic inputs; SHA-256: `e0214e1de6978b074042a07a1bb0327a5bee823b6dc71f2cd99d8800126f0032`.
This command deliberately exits 2 while electrical release requirements remain open.
A geometry pass cannot override this hold. No Gerbers are generated.

## Simple adapter circuit

Selected controller: **Seeed Studio XIAO SAMD21 (original, not Plus)**, official ZMK target
`seeeduino_xiao//zmk`. [ZMK hardware list](https://zmk.dev/docs/hardware),
[Seeed documentation](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/Seeeduino-XIAO/).
Left scan bank uses D1–D5; right uses D6–D10. No Bluetooth is needed.
The two banks have separate signal nets; only connector shells/TVS returns share
adapter GND. XIAO's existing normal USB port supplies its power and PC connection.

Adapter: two six-pin XIAO headers, two USB4115-03-C receptacles, ten mandatory
1k GPIO series resistors, twenty 1k contact-isolation resistors, ten
TPD1E05U06DYA TVS diodes. No LDO, charge pump, reference, active protector,
external pull-up or separate power supply. D0 and 5V header pins are omitted;
3V3 header contact is NC. Mount the XIAO after depaneling: its body overhangs
the narrow carrier. Minimum header standoff proposal is 3 mm; purchased hardware
and complete case Z clearance remain manual.

Each passive half has 20 switches/20 matrix diodes, one receptacle, five mandatory
1k GPIO resistors, ten 1k contact-isolation resistors and five TVS diodes.
Parsed schematic wires, labels, explicit NCs and PCB pad nets match for both boards.
There are **no copper tracks, vias or zones**; this is component placement/net assignment.

## Selected contact groups and four cable orientations

- Connector group 1: A2 + B2
- Connector group 2: A3 + B3
- Connector group 3: A10 + B10
- Connector group 4: A11 + B11
- Connector group 5: A8 + B8

Each contact passes through its **own 1k resistor before joining its group**.
Directly shorting an orientation pair could otherwise short two external host
SuperSpeed lanes without traversing the shared GPIO resistor. Between two such
contacts the proposed circuit supplies 2k resistance; it does not establish a
universal safe fault current for unspecified host voltages or ESD events.

The ideal passive full-featured cable model follows
[USB-IF Type-C R2.0 table 3-10, printed p75](https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/USB%20Type-C%20Spec%20R2.0%20-%20August%202019_0.pdf).
A/B reversal exchanges equal-index receptacle contacts. Physical connector group
crossing is always 1↔4, 2↔3, 5→5. On each adapter port groups 1–5 connect to
logical bank lines P3, P2, P1, P0, P4 to compensate. Every socket uses the same
physical contact groups; every half is electrically identical.

| Adapter plug | Half plug | Half lines reached from logical MCU P0–P4 (1-based) | Independent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | Normal | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | Yes |
| Normal | Reversed | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | Yes |
| Reversed | Normal | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | Yes |
| Reversed | Reversed | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | Yes |

The user's original cable-mate groups are preserved in the source as a regression
fixture: they swap identities when exactly one plug is reversed. The authorized
same-index grouping is applied to all three actual receptacles. Only passive,
full-featured USB 3.x C–C cables are modeled; USB2-only and active cables are unsupported.
Physical continuity with actual cables in all four orientations remains pending.

## Unused contacts and protection

All receptacle VBUS, CC1/CC2, USB2 D+/D− and GND contacts are explicitly NC:
A1, A12, B1, B12, A4, A9, B4, B9, A5, B5, A6, B6, A7, B7. No CC termination, VBUS power path or USB negotiation is
implemented on the split ports. These ports carry raw GPIO.
Adapter shell stakes connect to GND_A; half shell stakes and TVS return connect
to SHIELD_H. Cable plugs bond shell/shield and ground, so NC ground contacts do
**not** imply galvanic isolation. A half connected alone has no separate earth return.

The [GCT USB4115 manufacturer drawing](https://gct.co/files/drawings/usb4115.pdf) supplies the
24-contact numbering, 0.5 mm pitch, two pad rows 1.66 mm apart, 0.30×0.85 mm SMD
lands, four Ø0.70 mm shell stake holes and two Ø0.70 mm plastic locating holes.
Our shell copper pads are enlarged to Ø1.20 mm for a 0.25 mm ring. This is an
**upright 9.3 mm tall connector**, requiring case and cable access review.

[TI TPD1E05U06 data sheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd1e05u06.pdf)
describes the selected low-capacitance TVS. Its working/clamp ratings do not
make it a 3.3 V GPIO voltage limiter. Series resistance plus TVS provides basic
protection only: powered-off rail backfeed, MCU pin voltage/current limits,
negative faults, connector bridging, hot-plug and system ESD remain unqualified.
No dummy resistor, clamp or NC assignment is represented as guaranteed misplug immunity.

| Event | Intended mitigation | Open verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PC/charger to half | No VBUS/CC/USB2 path; resistor on every signal contact | Host lane loading with keys held, transients and shell return |
| PC/charger to adapter split port | Same NCs; contact and GPIO resistors; TVS to GND | Powered/unpowered MCU limits and backfeed; TVS clamp adequacy |
| Half to XIAO normal USB | No split-side CC or VBUS path | Exact module port/cable continuity and transients |
| Left/right cable exchanged | Separate interchangeable ports; identical halves | Hand assignment becomes the adapter port's assignment |
| Either plug reversed | Fixed cable crossing compensated at adapter | Actual cable continuity in all four orientations |
| Keys held during insert/remove | Series resistance; firmware must initialize high impedance | Contact sequencing, output interlock, hot-plug tests |

## Scan resistance and rollover

A complete key loop has four mandatory 1k GPIO resistors. Per signal, two parallel
cable conductors each include a 1k contact resistor at each end: (1k+1k)∥(1k+1k)
=1k. Sense and sink add another 2k, making **6k total**, excluding cable/contact
resistance and diode. All ten signal contacts must be connected by a full-featured cable.

[Microchip SAM D21 DS40001882L table 37-15](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/MCU32/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/SAM-D21-DA1-Family-Data-Sheet-DS40001882.pdf) specifies
20/40/60k internal pull-up min/typ/max and VILmax=0.3VDD. This is an illustrative
single-key screen at 3.3V, Vf=0.6V, optimistic VOL=0, without resistor tolerance,
leakage, ADC acquisition, shared sink currents or temperature bounds:

| Pull-up | Current | Vsense | VILmax | LOW margin |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20k | 103.8µA | 1.223V | 0.990V | -0.233V |
| 40k | 58.7µA | 0.952V | 0.990V | 0.038V |
| 60k | 40.9µA | 0.845V | 0.990V | 0.145V |

At 20k the key does not have a guaranteed digital LOW. A weak pull-up or ADC
algorithm is a possible follow-up, not an applied or proven solution.
The [stock ZMK charlieplex scanner](https://github.com/zmkfirmware/zmk/blob/main/app/module/drivers/kscan/kscan_gpio_charlieplex.c) uses digital
reads and internal pull-ups. Selecting a ZMK-supported MCU does **not** establish
that this resistor/diode network works with that driver.

Two held closures P0→P1 and P1→P2 also create a forward P0→P2 path. The executable
reachability witness verifies topology only, not that a two-diode path crosses
a particular threshold. Diode current/temperature curves, tolerances, sink sharing
and all-chord scan behavior need a defined driver and prototype measurements.
ADC-capable pins alone do not prove ghost-free rollover.

## Required before release

- The 6k closed-key loop lacks guaranteed digital-low margin with the minimum internal pull-up.
- Forward multi-key paths exist; scan method and measured rollover margins remain unresolved.
- Passive resistors and TVS do not guarantee GPIO overvoltage, powered-off backfeed or hot-plug safety.
- Actual cable continuity, powered/unpowered fault and board-level ESD qualification are pending.
- PCB is unrouted; native KiCad ERC/DRC and Gerber review have not run.

The user requested a simple adapter. Active rail/protection experiments have been
removed from the design. If passive protection cannot meet the required fault
cases, that limitation must be resolved explicitly before fabrication; no extra
power circuit is silently added. No manufacturer contact, order or publication occurred.
